title: Inspector shows incorrect Make Unique / linked state for Resources inside exported arrays in inherited scenes
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.6.2.stable, v4.7.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.3) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Pro (Apple7) - Apple M1 Pro (8 threads) - 32.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When a parent scene has an exported array containing Resources, and only one element is made unique and edited in an inherited child scene, the Inspector display no longer matches the actual shared state.

The Make Unique / linked state buttons shown for array elements do not correctly represent the actual resource sharing state.

**As far as I tested, this issue can be reproduced with the following Resource types:**
- Custom Resource
- Material
- Shape
- Other Resource types in general

**Script used**

```
extends Node
# Reproduction script confirmed with Material.
# The same issue was also observed with other Resource types,
# such as Array[CustomResource] and Array[Shape3D].
@export var motor_configs: Array[Material] = []

```

### Steps to reproduce

**[Steps to reproduce]**
1: Attach the script above to a parent scene and assign multiple Resources to Array[Material]
2: Create an inherited child scene from that parent scene
3: In the child scene, make only one element in the array unique and edit it
4: Save the child scene
5: Open the parent scene and check the Inspector display
6: Switch back and forth between the parent and child scenes while checking the Make Unique / linked state buttons for the array elements
7: Save when necessary and check how the display changes compared to the actual sharing state


**[Actual behavior]**
- Even though only one element was made unique, other elements may also appear editable
- Make Unique / linked state buttons may appear on elements that were not explicitly made unique
- The presence or absence of those buttons may change after saving or switching between parent and child scenes
- Some elements may appear localized, but are actually still shared between parent and child
- The button display may not match the actual shared state

N/A
